input:
You are bishop_c8, one of sixteen agents playing Black in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 20... the team planned Bxc4 (bishop_c8), and queen_d8 (greed) sent Qxa3, bishop_c8 (amnesia) sent Bxh3 instead. The contract refused them, and Bxc4 was played.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 11... the team planned Nxf5 (knight_b8), but knight_b8 (amnesia) sent Ng6 instead, and that move was played, costing 448 centipawns.
- On move 14... the team planned Kf8 (king_e8), and bishop_c8 (greed) sent Bxh3 instead. The contract refused it, and Kf8 was played.
- On move 15... the team planned Qxf6 (queen_d8), and bishop_f8 (greed) sent Bxf6 instead. The contract refused it, and Qxf6 was played.
- On move 17... the team planned Qd3 (queen_d8), and bishop_f8 (greed) sent Bxc3, bishop_c8 (greed) sent Bxh3 instead. The contract refused them, and Qd3 was played.
- On move 19... the team planned Be6 (bishop_c8), and bishop_c8 (amnesia) sent Bf5 instead. The contract refused it, and Be6 was played.

How your team coordinates: through a Modality contract. A Black move counts only when a commit that posts it to /moves/<agent>.text, the path of the piece that moves (and the ply to /turn/ply.num), is accepted. The referee plays the first accepted commit for each ply and reads nothing else.

The keys of all sixteen Black agents are at /team/pieces/<agent>.id. The contract already has the rule always([+modifies(/moves/$k.text) -signed_by(/team/pieces/$k.id)] false), where $k stands for every agent: only a piece can propose its own move. You don't need to write that rule again. When the team agrees on a plan, the piece that moves signs its commit and every agent that agrees co-signs, usually twelve to sixteen of you. An agent that goes off plan signs its own commit alone.

The contract accepts a commit only if it meets every rule in the contract. Any commit that meets the rules can add a rule, and a rule can never be removed.

Contract rules now:
- Any commit that modifies a /moves/<agent>.text path must be signed by at least twelve of the sixteen agents' keys in /team/pieces/, including the moving piece itself, so a lone off-plan move (panic, greed, or amnesia) cannot be accepted.
- Any commit that modifies /moves/knight_b8.text, /moves/bishop_c8.text, or /moves/bishop_f8.text, the pieces that have already gone off plan, must be signed by at least fourteen of the sixteen agents' keys in /team/pieces/, including the moving piece itself.
- Any commit that modifies /moves/bishop_c8.text or /moves/bishop_f8.text, the two bishops that keep going off plan through greed, must be signed by all sixteen of the sixteen agents' keys in /team/pieces/, so a bishop's move is accepted only with unanimous team agreement.
- Any commit that modifies /moves/knight_b8.text (the piece whose amnesia move was actually played and cost 448 centipawns) must be signed by all sixteen of the sixteen agents' keys in /team/pieces/, including knight_b8 itself, so that no move for that piece is accepted without unanimous team agreement.

A rule can cover the whole team or a single agent. For example, a rule can ask for more signatures on one agent's path, /moves/<agent>.text, if that agent keeps going off plan.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule, in plain language, to add to the contract that would help your team win. It will be turned into a Modality formula, so it must be about signatures, paths, or values in the contract.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>"}
response: {"rule": "Any commit that modifies /moves/queen_d8.text must be signed by at least fourteen of the sixteen agents' keys in /team/pieces/, including queen_d8 itself, because queen_d8 has repeatedly gone off plan through greed, and every commit that modifies any /moves/<agent>.text path must also modify /turn/ply.num so a move only counts for the ply it was planned for."}
